Queen Elizabeth II passed away on September 8, 2022, at Balmoral Castle in Scotland. Her death was officially announced by Buckingham Palace at 6:30 PM BST. She had been under medical supervision earlier that day, and her immediate family members rushed to be by her side.

The Queen's death marked the end of the longest reign in British history, spanning over 70 years. She ascended to the throne on February 6, 1952, following the death of her father, King George VI. Throughout her seven decades of service, she witnessed tremendous social, political, and technological changes.

The day after her death, September 9, began a period of national mourning that lasted for 12 days. Her state funeral was held at Westminster Abbey on September 21, 2022, attended by over 2,000 guests, including heads of state and dignitaries from around the world. Following the ceremony, she was laid to rest in St. George's Chapel at Windsor Castle, alongside her beloved husband Prince Philip, who had passed away in April 2021.

Queen Elizabeth II passed away on September 8, 2022, at Balmoral Castle in Scotland. The announcement of her death came at 6:30 PM BST, after members of the royal family had rushed to be by her side earlier that day. Her death marked the end of the longest reign in British history, spanning over 70 years. Earlier that week, she had formally appointed Liz Truss as the new Prime Minister, making this her final public duty. In the hours following her death, Operation London Bridge was activated, initiating a carefully planned sequence of events. Prince Charles immediately became King upon her death, though his formal coronation ceremony wasn't held until May 4, 2023, in Westminster Cathedral, where he chose to wear the same crown his mother had worn during her coronation in 1952. The funeral procession drew over 4 million spectators to central London, making it one of the largest public gatherings in British history.
Queen Elizabeth II died on September 8, 2022, at Balmoral Castle in Scotland. She was 96 years old and had reigned for 70 years, making her the longest-reigning British monarch in history.
